rules.rule: To show that you actually read the paper, explain how the study design was implemented, not just the abstract-level conclusion.
rules.reason: The professor explicitly said the point of assigning the paper was to see how the research design taught in class was implemented in a real article.

rules.rule: Separate cohort difference from age difference, and separate performance level from rate of decline.
rules.reason: The discussion repeatedly emphasized that later-born cohorts performing higher is not the same claim as declining more slowly, and that the paper compares cohorts within the same age range.

rules.rule: When discussing cognitive aging, do not treat cognition as one ability; explain the domain-specific pattern.
rules.reason: The professor highlighted that cognitive aging must be read by domain because different abilities peak and decline differently.

rules.rule: Use the exact paper variables and do not collapse work control, work autonomy, and work innovation into one vague job-quality idea.
rules.reason: The class focused on the fact that the three work-environment variables behaved differently, especially that autonomy did not show the same cohort pattern as control and innovation.

rules.rule: If you connect the paper to the Flynn effect, explain the connection carefully instead of treating them as identical claims.
rules.reason: The professor used the Flynn effect to clarify the idea of later-born cohorts scoring higher, but not as a complete substitute for the paper?s own argument.

rules.rule: Do not stop at the main finding; also mention causal-direction limits and the paper?s own limitations.
rules.reason: The discussion explicitly raised whether enriched work improves cognition or cognitively stronger people enter such work, and pointed students to the limitation section as part of real paper reading.

rules.rule: If you say the result was interesting or surprising, explain what you expected before reading and what changed after reading.
rules.reason: The professor pushed students to move beyond bare reaction and state the prior expectation they revised.
